title: 7 Colts players, including several starters, inactive v. Texans - Yahoo Sports
content: The Indianapolis Colts are listing seven players as inactive for Thursday's matchup with the Houston Texans. On game days, teams are permitted to have only 48 players active and available. On Wednesday, the Colts announced that TE Will Mallory (hamstring), OT Bernhard Raimann (concussion), defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf), OT Jalen Travis (knee), and CB Charvarius Ward (knee) would all be out. Gardner (calf) was originally listed as questionable. He did not practice during the week. The Colts will be without their two starting tackles, likely leaving Matt Goncalves to start at right tackle and Luke Tenuta at left tackle. Kenneth Harris and Justin Walley are candidates to line up at outside CB. Kapena Gushiken could handle slot snaps if Walley isn't lining up there. Tim Smith saw more snaps at DT against Miami, as did Kevin Givens. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: 7 Colts players, including several starters, inactive v. Texans

title: Could Grand Theft Auto VI become a problem for NHL players? A former goalie blamed GTA V for his worst season. - RMNB
content: The video-game world saw the most-anticipated game in history get released on Thursday. Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar Games’ answer to Grand Theft Auto V 13 years later, officially hit shelves and has received nearly universal critical praise. The game earned a 99/100 on Metacritic, as millions of gamers have rushed to explore the sprawling new version of Vice City. The launch has also been a massive commercial success, at least according to early estimates. Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that GTA VI had sold more than 19 million copies, as reported by Reuters, and generated approximately $1.84 billion in revenue by Thursday morning. The excitement has been so widespread that fans have taken time off work and stayed up through the night to play. While the game has no real connection to sports, one former goaltender believes it may affect the NHL, and his opinion is backed by personal experience. Craig Anderson, a veteran of 709 NHL games with the Chicago Blackhawks, Florida Panthers, Colorado Avalanche, Ottawa Senators, Washington Capitals, and Buffalo Sabres, recently made an appearance on the Absolute Non-Sens podcast and spoke about his belief that Grand Theft Auto V, released in September 2013, contributed to his worst season with the Senators. Anderson played parts of 10 seasons with Ottawa from 2010-2020. “My worst season, speaking of video games and how it can be either a detriment or a non-detriment, my worst season that I felt that I had in Ottawa was the year that Grand Theft Auto V came out,” Anderson said. “Direct correlation between, let’s say, just the time suck of, you know, you’d play after a game. You get home. (at) 11:00, 11:30, and you’d start playing that game, and it’d be 4:00 am, and you’d be like, I’m not even tired. “And now Grand Theft Auto VI is coming out, so it’ll be interesting to see how that all plays out. But for me, video games is a huge thing for me. I felt like I wasn’t able to separate. Like I said, one of my worst seasons here was getting sucked into that a little bit too much.” During the 2013-14 campaign, Anderson went 25-16-8 with a 3.00 goals-against average, a .911 save percentage, and four shutouts. While those numbers don’t seem all that poor, they were compared to his prior season with the team, where he had a 1.69 GAA, a .941 save percentage, and three shutouts in just 24 appearances. Anderson struggled particularly in November 2013, going just 2-4-0 with a 4.00 GAA and a .866 save percentage. He gave up four or more goals in five of his seven starts that month. Getting lost in the new game, just as Anderson did in the prior installment, will be easy. Consider this example: the game has so much detail that you can actually find and sell football cards at a Vice City pawn shop. GTA 6 footage shows COLLECTIBLE football cards that you can actually find and sell at pawn shops! The amount of detail in this game is INSANE. pic.twitter.com/MtyYhFoGt6 The topic of video games impacting athlete performance has come up in the NHL before, with Patrik Laine taking heat early in his career for what was deemed an obsession with Fortnite. Laine was reportedly so into the game that he almost played every day, even taking it on the road with him and choosing to stay in hotels instead of going out to eat with his teammates. GTA VI: Jumbotron edition 🎮 pic.twitter.com/F7pUgFeFyJ Given the open-world nature and 60-plus-hour story in GTA VI, the game is being brought up as a potential distraction for pros in all sports, even reaching Washington Capitals head coach Spencer Carbery on Thursday morning. Carbery was asked by 106.7 The Fan’s Sports Junkies whether he knew if any Capitals players planned to indulge in the newest gaming fad. “I’m going to get to the bottom of that,” Carbery said. “I know we have a bunch of gamers on our team. I don’t know who will be specifically playing Grand Theft Auto, but I’ll poke around today.” The Capitals do have a few noted gamers among their ranks, with rookie defenseman Cole Hutson and winger Ryan Leonard previously discussing their own Fortnite gameplay sessions. The team’s captain, Alex Ovechkin, was also known to don a gaming headset in the past. Whether any of them plan to take control of GTA VI’s main protagonists, Jason and Lucia, in Rockstar’s Vice City remains unknown. title: Menlo Vet C.C. Gong Moves to Quash UMG v. Suno Subpoena - Digital Music News
content: The former Menlo employee just recently took aim at the testimony demand with a firmly worded motion to quash. As many know from our in-depth coverage, the subpoenas are flying in UMG v. Suno, where related disputes are unfolding with non-parties including the MLC, Apple, and multiple investors. Among those investors is the Suno Series C lead and Series D participant Menlo. At the outset, its subpoena included a question concerning Gong’s aforesaid February 2026 tweet, which appears significant from the perspective of the platform’s fair-use defense and the majors’ market-dilution claims. (“I’ve personally shifted most of my listening to Suno,” she wrote in part. “I was so tired of Spotify giving me the same overplayed recommendations. When everyone can create, the catalog becomes infinite and music becomes more personalized. Instead of competing for mainstream hits, AI unlocks an ever-expanding long tail, meaning everyone can find their song, not just a song.”) Fast forward to mid-October, when the litigating majors say they first learned that Gong had left Menlo at September’s end. The information promptly spurred an additional third-party subpoena seeking testimony from Gong herself and evidently set the stage for a good bit of discussion between the parties. (Furthermore, in part because Gong is said to have a “busy” travel schedule, DMN’s coverage arrived nine days before she was actually served.) Besides actively negotiating this deposition’s suitable sub-topics (Gong’s posting and deleting the tweet, Menlo’s knowledge thereof, etc.), the majors have simultaneously been pushing to compel Gong’s testimony as well. The way Lewis & Llewellyn-repped Gong’s attorneys tell the story, something of a compromise was on the table one week ago: She would sit for a one-hour remote deposition “in her individual capacity” and address her “personal reasons for posting and deleting the social media post and her personal music-listening habits.” Plus, Menlo’s own witness would be grilled on the non-personal reasons and information behind the post. “The likely explanation for Plaintiffs’ four-hour demand is that they intend to use Ms. Gong’s deposition to explore not just her tweet and personal listening habits, but also subjects assigned to Menlo’s corporate representative and even matters unrelated to the tweet altogether,” Gong’s counsel added. Getting down to it, then, the ex-Menlo higher-up maintains that the subpoena “exclusively seeks testimony that is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative” and “is harassment for the sake of potential litigation advantage.” Moreover, the possible benefits of deposing her “about a single tweet would be outweighed by the substantial burden on her time and potential disruption to her travel schedule,” according to the filing, which proceeds to allege that Universal Music and Sony Music should have gotten the ball rolling some time back. The majors “had seven months before discovery closed to serve Ms. Gong with a deposition subpoena, but waited until after the close of fact discovery to seek leave to take Ms. Gong’s deposition,” per the legal text, emphasizing for good measure that “they could have subpoenaed her at any point between February 26 and October 2, 2026.” For these reasons, the court should quash the subpoena – or green-light “an order modifying it to limit her deposition to one hour on the record and to limit questioning to her February 2026 tweet,” the motion concludes.

title: 44k-Mile 2004 Cadillac CTS-V With a Six-Speed Is Bidding at $10,250 With No Reserve - Motorious
content: Classic car news, hand-picked vehicles, and auction coverage. Choose what lands in your inbox. Before Cadillac's V-Series became a household name among enthusiasts, there was one clean-sheet idea: put a Corvette Z06 engine in a rear-drive luxury sedan and bolt a stick shift to it. A 44k-mile 2004 Cadillac CTS-V is up for auction on Hagerty Marketplace, offered with no reserve, and it makes a strong case for why the original still matters. The bidding sits at $10,250 after 25 bids, with the auction scheduled to end Monday, November 23, at 2:35 p.m. EST. Because there's no reserve, the highest bidder when the clock runs out takes the car. The 2004 CTS-V was the debut of Cadillac's V-Series performance division, built on General Motors' rear-wheel-drive Sigma platform and aimed squarely at European sport sedans. The listing reports first-year production of 2,509 units, which helps explain why clean, low-mileage examples draw attention today. Under the hood is the 5.7-liter LS6 V8, the same family of engine used in the Corvette Z06, factory-rated at 400 horsepower. It sends power to the rear wheels through a TREMEC T56 six-speed manual, a combination that's become increasingly hard to find in a four-door luxury car. A limited-slip rear differential, performance-tuned suspension and steering, and Brembo brakes at all four corners round out the performance hardware. This example is finished in black over a black interior and shows 44,100 miles on the odometer. The seller says they bought it from the original owner in 2020. Equipment includes the CTS-V mesh grille and rear decklid spoiler, 18-inch cast aluminum wheels, xenon HID headlamps, a sunroof, power sport seats with driver's memory, dual-zone climate control and a leather-wrapped wheel and shift knob. The only listed modification is a Pioneer double-DIN radio, and the seller states that all equipment, including the sunroof, seats, mirrors and radio, is working. The car is offered with manufacturer's literature, a CARFAX Vehicle History Report and a clean Pennsylvania title in the seller's name. It's located in Orefield, Pennsylvania. The listing is upfront about the car's history. The CARFAX report notes damage to the driver's front in June 2020, and the seller says the driver-side doors and rear quarter panel were repaired by Gerber Collision and Glass. The seller also mentions four to five minor paint chips on the hood and some noise from the original shocks over bumps such as railroad tracks. Registration history shows New Jersey and Pennsylvania, with some reporting gaps, so prospective bidders will want to read the full CARFAX and do their own inspection, as Hagerty advises. A manual, V8, rear-drive sports sedan with this few miles is a combination the market rarely offers, and the first-year CTS-V sits at the start of a lineage that grew far more powerful in later generations. If you've been looking for a modern performance sedan you can actually enjoy driving, this one deserves a look before the hammer falls on Monday. title: GTA VI Release Day: Where Pirates Were When GTA V Dropped - Sports Illustrated
content: PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Pirates aren't playing right now, which isn't the worst thing with attention put elsewhere. Grand Theft Auto VI was released on Nov. 19, marking the eighth edition and the newest game from one of the most popular video game franchises ever. It's the first GTA since the fifth one came out in 2013, 13 years ago, and is finally out after many delays and postponements. 2013 was a different time for everyone, especially the Pirates, who were in one of the best recent stretches in team history. GTA V was released on Sept. 17, 2013, which marked the first season in two decades that the Pirates were successful. The Pirates had clinched their first winning season since 1992, after 20 consecutive seasons below .500, a record in North American professional sports. Pittsburgh earned its 82nd win on Sept. 9 in a 1-0 win over the Texas Rangers at the Ballpark in Arlington, but had ended its losing season streak on Sept. 3, with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers at Miller Park. The Pirates were 87-64, one game back of the St. Louis Cardinals in the National League Central Division and 1.5 games ahead in the Wild Card standings. Pittsburgh failed to win the division, as the Cardinals finished three games ahead, 97-65, for the best record in the NL. The Pirates did earn the fourth NL Wild Card spot, sweeping the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park the final weekend of the season. That sweep set up the first postseason game at PNC Park, with the Pirates hosting those Reds on Oct. 1, also the first postseason game for the Pirates since the 1992 NLCS. Outfielder Marlon Byrd and catcher Russell Martin hit solo home runs in the second inning, with the latter coming after the PNC Park-record crowd of 40,487 had chanted Reds' starting pitcher Johnny Cueto's name. The Pirates defeated the Reds 6-2 to advance to the NLDS, where they took on the Cardinals. Pittsburgh took a 2-1 lead in the NLDS, but couldn't close out the series, as the Cardinals won the final two games to move on to the NLCS. The Pirates earned two more NL Wild Card berths, but have never come close to that success since, with the second-longest postseason drought in MLB (2015). Center fielder Andrew McCutchen won the 2013 National League MVP, along with his third straight All-Star nod and second straight Silver Slugger Award. Third baseman Pedro Álvarez hit an NL-leading 36 home runs and won a Silver Slugger Award as well, making for two strong parts of the lineup. Pittsburgh had a strong rotation with veterans in Francisco Liriano, A.J. Burnett and Wandy Rodríguez, while 2011 first overall pick Gerrit Cole made his MLB debut and Charlie Morton had success. The Pirates bullpen was dominant, earning the nickname "The Shark Tank," with the likes of All-Star closer Jason Grilli, Mark Melancon, Tony Watson, Justin Wilson, Vin Mazzaro and Bryan Morris. It was one of the best seasons in recent Pirates history and one the franchise is hoping to emulate in 2027. None of the Pirates who finished the 2026 season were playing in MLB during the 2013 season, which includes relief pitcher Kirby Yates, who retired at 39. Starting pitcher Mitch Keller, the most senior Pirates player, was a senior at Xavier High School in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, less than a year before the Pirates selected him with the 64th overall pick in the second round of the 2014 MLB Draft. Outfielder Bryan Reynolds was a freshman at Vanderbilt and would soon help his team win the College World Series that spring, batting .338/.395/.480 for an OPS of .875. Relief pitcher Luke Weaver was readying for his junior season at Florida State, where he posted an 8-4 record in 16 starts with a 2.62 ERA and 92 strikeouts, before the Cardinals took him with the 27th pick in the first round in 2014. Fellow relief pitcher Lake Bachar was at Division III football powerhouse Wisconsin-Whitewater and eventually started playing baseball after his freshman year, doing so as a sophomore in 2015. First baseman Ryan O'Hearn was a junior with Sam Houston State, and would hit .292/.348/.451 for an OPS of .799, leading to the Kansas City Royals taking him in the eighth round of the 2014 draft. title: Iron Owl Day Four, Events V and VI - Florida Atlantic University Athletics
content:
BOCA RATON, Fla. – The Florida Atlantic baseball team held two Iron Owl events on Thursday, once again testing brains and strength.

Team Blue made a big jump on Thursday and is now just two points behind the two-day leader Columbia. Senior INF Ty Lagoni also usurped RHP James Litman on the individual leaderboard after Litman had led the competition much of the week. Two newcomers to the top five individual standings are senior RHP Kyzer Smith while junior C TJ Gramesty returned after losing his spot earlier in the week.

Thursday once again tested both the cerebral and athletic sides of the 2027 baseball team. Teams worked together to provide the answer in the form of a question and finished by calculating the wager, based on earlier game-winning to assure a victory. The afternoon was held in the Slattery Family Performance Center. Half was used for dodgeball; the other half used for two timed individual events. The first timed event was an iron cross, the second a plate hold.

While postseason honors are celebrated, the Iron Owl is a coveted award that debuted prior to the 2008 season. The goal is to foster team camaraderie while ensuring that each individual player understands what it is like to compete on a daily basis. The program aims for each player to reach their highest potential in the classroom, on the field and in the weight room. The award identifies the strongest Owl baseball player, both mentally and physically. In addition to team and individual competitions off the field, each player's GPA from the fall semester is also taken into account.

DAY FOUR
Day four began at 7 a.m. with Jeopardy, using answers relating to FAU baseball, music and assorted other questions. The Jeopardy competition was followed by an individual spelling bee. The squad then shifted to a 1 p.m. physical testing along with a friendly game of dodgeball, officiated by pitching coach and alum Hunter Cooley.

title: Obergefell v. Hodges is more than a precedent, it is peoples’ lives - The Badger Herald
content: To some, same-sex marriage may be seen as “just” a political issue, but many people’s real lives are at stake. As of today, same-sex marriage is legal in all 50 states thanks to Obergefell v. Hodges, which struck down state bans on same-sex marriage across all 50 states and Washington, D.C., in 2015. But, last year Kim Davis, a former county clerk in Kentucky who was sued in 2015 for refusing to issue marriage licenses because of her opposition to same-sex marriage based on her religious beliefs, called for the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn Obergefell v. Hodges. Thankfully, on Nov. 10, 2025, the Supreme Court denied the appeal and Obergefell v. Hodges stood. The denial was relieving, but the action of Davis and many others is disheartening. In the aftermath of the 2022 Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization decision, which overturned the landmark abortion rights decision, Roe v. Wade, some LGBTQ+ activists pointed to conservative Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas’ suggestion in his concurring opinion in the Dobbs decision, that Obergefell v. Hodges and some other cases should also be revisited, as a cause for concern. Same-sex marriage encapsulates two hallowed doctrines in U.S. constitutional law: marriage as a “fundamental right,” and equality as the key to shared freedom, according to SCOTUS Blog. Putting the two together gave us marriage equality at the heart of it all. Marriage as a legal matter is controlled by state law, meaning it is up to the states to decide who can marry. But, marriage is also a constitutional matter, which is how Obergefell v. Hodges was born. Historically, in 1888, the Supreme Court said marriage is “the most important relation in life” and “the foundation of the family and of society, without which there would be neither civilization nor progress,” according to SCOTUS Blog. In 1965, the Court described marriage as “an association that promotes a way of life, not causes; a harmony in living, not political faiths; a bilateral loyalty, not commercial or social projects,” according to SCOTUS Blog. The 2026 midterms highlighted the impact of the social environment when conservatives are in control. On Election Day in Virginia, Virginians voted 56% to remove the same-sex marriage ban from the state’s constitution according to The Trevor Project. This vote marks a major milestone as Virginia becomes the first southern state to enshrine marriage equality in its constitution. Queer and transgender candidates also made history by winning elections. Seventeen openly LGBTQ+ federal lawmakers were newly elected, including New Hampshire’s Chris Papas, the first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate, according to The Trevor Project. Protecting LGBTQ+ marriage rights goes hand in hand with electing people whose experiences are shared with those who they protect. LGBTQ+ marriage is more than just equal rights, and it should be considered a basic human right. Marriage, legally speaking, encapsulates more than just a piece of paper joining two people together. Marriage provides a mix of legal rights, financial protections and emotional security, which vary by state, that a non-married relationship does not automatically receive under the law. In Wisconsin, these include medical record access, inheritance and estate rights, tax advantages, insurance and employment perks and immigration benefits, along with public and shared identity and a psychological safety net. Before marriage equality was the law, lack of access to these protections placed extra strain on LGBTQ+ couples. Without Obergefell v. Hodges, long-term partners were unable to share in the pension survivor or Social Security benefits their partner or spouse had paid because they were not married and had no rights to a share of a deceased partner’s estate without a will, meaning a survivor could lose both their beloved partner and their financial security. Although couples shared bank and credit card accounts, bought property together and planned life together as one family, their invisibility as a legal family compelled them to pay for separate health insurance policies, to file separate federal income tax returns and to pay higher rates without the married filing jointly status or the ability to take or pool various deductions. In many states, couples were unable to obtain a court judgment of adoption or joint parentage that would secure both partners’ legal relationship with their child, among many other obstacles same-sex couples face without marriage rights. While the Supreme Court has, for now, shown no indication that it is seeking to overturn Obergefell v. Hodges, in the last decade it has shown a tendency to strengthen religious rights at the expense of LGBTQ+ rights. With the 2026 midterm results, LGBTQ+ marriage may be protected for now. But, same-sex marriage should not only be seen as “just” a political issue used within liberal vs. conservative arguments. title: Down – V Review - Angry Metal Guy
content: The legendary DOWN formed in 1991 in New Orleans, Louisiana, featuring an esteemed pedigree, including members of Pantera, Eyehategod, Crowbar, and Corrosion of Conformity. Living up to the dreaded and often underwhelming supergroup tag, DOWN unloaded their classic NOLA debut in 1995, a high-water mark release and stoner-sludge masterpiece. DOWN re-emerged on 2002’s underrated Down II: A Bustle in your Hedgerow, a more refined, experimental, and sprawling psychedelia-tinged opus. Over the Under dropped in 2007 to solid if mixed results, before DOWN pumped out the stripped-back and uniformly solid pair of IV EPs in 2012 and 2014. As the years marched on, the prospect of the grizzled veterans returning to the studio seemed to fade, before finally returning for their misleadingly titled V album, the acclaimed band’s fourth LP. In the twilight of their hard living years, can the current lineup of Phil Anselmo (Pantera, Superjoint), bassist Pat Bruders (Crowbar, Goatwhore), drummer Jimmy Bower (Eyehategod, Superjoint) and legendary guitarists Kirk Windstein (Crowbar) and Pepper Keenan (Corrosion of Conformity) rekindle the fire? Approaching V with a sense of trepidation, any concerns of DOWN sounding tired or washed up are emphatically squashed on opener “The Myth,” a burly, hard-rocking starter built upon heavy-duty grooves and sprightly, infectious sludge doom riffs. Essentially, reintroducing Down’s classic sound for the modern era, an infectious, appropriately beefy call to arms. Fellow single “Bood Oath” burns slowly before unfurling into a righteous sludge-doom riff monster, built on granite-block riffs, a classic NOLA swagger, and commanding Anselmo vocals. DOWN sound well and truly dialed in and reinvigorated on their return, retaining the signature elements of their classic sound, boosted by a beefy production and modern kick. Bruder’s thick low end and Bowers’ intuitive, groove-centric drumming hammer home a tight rhythmic base for the dual axework of Windstein and Keenan to unload a deft and rugged supply of top-notch riffs and rich harmonies, informed by sludge, doom, and bluesy southern rock influences. Running nearly an hour long, V does things by full measures, with four cuts leaning into longer-form seven-minute-plus lengths. Thankfully, the material stretches across a varied palette without straining too far from DOWN’s classic stoner doom-sludge roots. Amidst the downtrodden, bluesy sludge and adventurous songwriting, reside more straightforward, riffy sluggers (“Turn Out the Light,” “The Message”), creating an infectiously dynamic to-and-fro. Early on, listeners are treated to the cheekily titled “Merciful Fate,” the first of the longer-form ditties. Even resident curmudgeon Doc Grier would be tickled pink by the effectively understated guest spot from the legendary King Diamond and wife Livia Zita, adding an eerie and theatrical charm as Phil reminisces on hard living pasts and uncertain futures across a smartly arranged sludge-doom epic. “Ozz” pays heartfelt tribute to the late, great Ozzy Osbourne; its folksy atmospheric vibes evoke memories of “Planet Caravan” and “Suicide Note, Pt 1,” though in less bleak terms. It’s a refreshing outlier, only marred by awkward phrasing and heavy-handed lyricism. Parts of V are a tad long in the tooth, though it sags in segments, rather than being bogged down by excessive weight. In fact, some of V’s strongest moments feature on the lengthier cuts. For instance, the immense “Causeway Grief” forms a powerhouse slice of doom, driven by a crushing, melancholic weight, gritty, soulful Anselmo vocal, and bruising, smoldering guitar work. Meanwhile, “They Walk the Night” follows a raucous, groovier path, featuring enough crunchy riffs, dynamic shifts, and vocal hooks to keep pace with its length. Most material lands, and there are no outright duds. Problematic issues include some sequencing quibbles, minor bloat, and the odd stock moment or clunky lyric. Issues are relatively minor when stacked against the album’s quality riffcraft and songwriting, resulting in a sturdy and addictive comeback platter. Detractors of Anselmo’s vocal performances over the years will find a hard time building a case against Phil here. Naturally, his voice has become rougher and weathered over time; however, the power and emotion behind his distinctive pipes sound both authoritative and inspired. Wisely, Anselmo mostly sticks within the limitations of his current range. Unfortunately, it’s not his finest hour lyrically. V is both a pleasant surprise and triumphant return from DOWN, exceeding admittedly tame expectations and largely rising above its flaws and bloated length. Twenty-twenty-six has been an especially fruitful year for the veteran class, and DOWN’s rejuvenated and punchy comeback ticks a lot of boxes, adding a seasoned, strong entry to their esteemed legacy. ﻿ Rating: 3.5/5.0 DR: 6 | Format Reviewed: 256 kbps mp3 Label: Nuclear Blast Websites: Facebook | Official Releases Worldwide: November 20th, 2026 "Supergroups. title: Washington Spirit v Kansas City Current: where the NWSL Championship will be won and lost - The Guardian
content: Croix Bethune, Trinity Rodman and the Rowdy Audi crowd are among the factors that could swing Saturday’s final This year’s NWSL Championship blends recurring themes with some newness. For the familiar: the Washington Spirit are in the final for the third straight year, hoping the third time’s the charm after back-to-back 1-0 defeats in their past two attempts. Slightly familiar, too, is Kansas City Current playing the championship game at Washington’s Audi Field, where they lost the final to Portland in 2022 and where they will contend again Saturday. For the novelty? Neither Kansas City nor Washington, despite their modern dominance in the NWSL table, have won the championship since 2021 (when Washington won). With Gotham’s bid for a two-peat stymied by the Current in the semi-final, here are five things that will decide a new winner in 2026. Washington’s defensive pressure Washington have allowed the second-fewest goals in the NWSL this year. Through the season and into the playoffs, the center-back pairing of the English defender Esme Morgan and Tara Rudd, the Scottish goalkeeper Sandy MacIver (fourth-highest save percentage in NWSL) and the defensive midfielder Andi Sullivan have been tough to break through for even the league’s most elite attackers. Further up the field, the Spirit’s defense begins with an attacking unit fond of forcing mistakes that lead to goals, with the late-season addition of Clara Luvanga (who has seven goal contributions in seven games for the Spirit) a key impact. Kansas City, who have scored more goals than any other NWSL team this year, will be a challenge. Defending set pieces will be a space to watch, as they provided the only goal Utah scored against the Spirit in the semi-final, and all the goals Kansas City scored against Gotham. Bethune on a mission against former team This season’s Midfielder of the Year is representing a team in the NWSL Championship for the third straight year (her second with availability to play). But this will be her first not representing the Spirit. After leaving Washington for Missouri in February, Bethune is facing her former team for the chance to win her first championship trophy. A bit more poetry: Bethune nearly broke the NWSL’s all-time single-season assists record during her 2024 rookie season for the Spirit. (A torn meniscus cut short her streak, but she still was named Rookie of the Year.) She finally broke it this season with Kansas City. Her creative influence in the Current’s midfield has been crucial to unlocking their goal-scoring capabilities. Bethune’s ability to pull apart Washington’s laudable defensive structure could prove crucial in the final. Kansas City’s attacking depth Temwa Chawinga is a two-time NWSL MVP for a reason, but she wasn’t the sole source of Kansas City’s 54 goals in 30 regular season games. The Current’s past nine goals (across five games including the playoffs) were scored by six different players, with Haley Hopkins (tied with Chawinga for goal contributions in the regular season) notching four of them. Chawinga enters the Championship with only one goal contribution in five games and no goals since 3 October, but she can break through at any moment. If not, the Current’s surrounding cast of contributors – Hopkins, Michelle Cooper, Bethune and Debinha – seems prepared to make the difference. Rodman is the Spirit’s gamechanger The Spirit also have attacking depth, but Rodman is a gamechanger whose impact is more lopsided. Her 20 goal contributions in the regular season were more than double the goal contributions of any teammate, and that’s without quantifying the space she frees up for fellow goalscorers with her calculated off-the-ball movements. In the postseason, Rodman has four goal contributions in two games – two goals and two assists. Coming at the end of one of her best club seasons, a big performance in the final will be essential for a Spirit victory. It would also further solidify her as one of the deserved main characters (and highest-paid player) in the NWSL. No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Will Rowdy Audi make a difference? Stadium squabbles were an unexpected storyline of this year’s postseason. Gotham and Washington faced scheduling hurdles that called into question their home-field advantage and/or forced them to play on less-than-ideal pitches for their semi-finals. But this Saturday, the Spirit will still have home-field advantage at Audi Field, where they’ve earned the trust of a robust home crowd. Whether Washington can turn that familiar, friendly space into the perfect scene for actually lifting the trophy in their third straight final would be a poetic end to the postseason’s stadium woes. title: Revisiting sports and pop culture from GTA V's launch - ESPN
content: Peyton Manning was beginning a record-setting season. Joel Embiid had yet to play a college basketball game. And "Breaking Bad" hadn't reached its finale. That was 4,812 days ago, when "Grand Theft Auto V" arrived on Sept. 17, 2013. More than 13 years later, "Grand Theft Auto VI" launches Thursday, with athletes and teams counting down to its release -- and looking back at how much has changed. Houston Rockets center Steven Adams even quipped during media day that performances could be impacted by the game's release. "So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet. Just for the month of November, performances are going to go down," Adams said. Before finding out whether Adams' prediction holds up, here's a look at the sports and pop culture landscape when GTA V arrived -- Sept. 17, 2013. The NFL had just finished its second week and two squads were in the early stages of dominant campaigns: Seattle and Denver. The Seahawks' defense proved to be its superpower, earning the "Legion of Boom" nickname. Seattle allowed 273.6 yards and 14.4 points per game, both the fewest in the regular season. The Broncos averaged a league-high 457.3 yards and 37.9 points per game, while Peyton Manning tossed an NFL record 5,477 yards plus 55 touchdowns. Both teams would finish with 13-3 records, setting up a Super Bowl meeting in February 2014. Seattle would emerge victorious on the biggest stage after stifling Denver's offense in a 43-8 victory -- and the seeds of Super Bowl XLVIII were sprouting as GTA V was released. The LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh Big Three were entering their fourth season as teammates following back-to-back titles. Miami edged out the San Antonio Spurs in the 2013 NBA Finals, an instant classic. The Heat faced a series clinching defeat in Game 6 before Ray Allen's late 3-pointer sent it into overtime. The extra period ended in a Miami victory to force a Game 7, where it closed out another championship. The Heat faced the Spurs in a rematch in 2014, and San Antonio got its revenge this time around. But, for two straight summers, Miami reigned supreme. The 2013 college basketball freshman class had its fair share of heavy hitters. In March 2013, then-high schoolers Andrew Wiggins and Jabari Parker graced the cover of Slam Magazine with the headline "Young Money: The game's next superstars have arrived." Wiggins and Parker were No. 1 and 2, respectively, in the SC Next rankings, but they were far from the only top prospects. Joel Embiid, Julius Randle and Aaron Gordon all featured in the top 10 of the rankings as five-star prospects. Each of them, alongside Wiggins and Parker, went one-and-done and were selected in the top 10 of the 2014 NBA draft. Other notable names in the 2013 high school class included twins Aaron and Andrew Harrison, Noah Vonleh and Wayne Selden. One of the greatest TV shows of all time, the final season of "Breaking Bad" aired as GTA V came out. Two days before its release, the iconic "Ozymandias" episode aired. Series creator Vince Gilligan said that the episode is the "best episode we ever have had or ever will have." It remains one of the highest-rated episodes of the series on IMDB with 9.5 stars. Pop songs led the way on the Billboard Hot 100 the week GTA V came out. Katy Perry's "Roar" hit No. 1 on Sept. 16, 2013, at the time matching Rihanna for the most No. 1's in the chart's 21-year history at 10. It took six weeks for "Roar" to reach No. 1, then-the fastest No. 1 hit since Perry's "California Gurls" in 2010. Slotted in at No. 2 was "Blurred Lines" by Robin Thicke featuring T.I. and Pharrell. That track spent 10 weeks on the top before being dethroned. Lorde's "Royals" was at No. 3, while Jay-Z and Justin Timberlake's "Holy Grail" sat at No. 4. The rest of the songs on the charts' top 10 included: "Wake Me Up!" by Avicii, "Summertime Sadness" by Lana Del Rey vs. Cedric Gervais, "Applause" by Lady Gaga, "Hold On, We're Going Home" by Drake featuring Majid Jordan, "Safe And Sound" by Capital Cities and "Berzerk" by Eminem. The Minnesota Lynx won their second WNBA championship in 2013, and it would mark the beginning of a dynasty. Minnesota won two more in 2015 and 2017, the latter of which made it four titles in seven seasons as the club also won in 2011. Hall of Famer Maya Moore played a key role in each of the four championships. In 2013, she averaged 20.9 points on 53% shooting in the playoffs. MLB saw similar dominance in alternating years from the San Francisco Giants. San Francisco missed the postseason in 2013 after World Series titles in 2010 and 2012. Someone privy to a trend could've predicted that the Giants would win it again in 2014 -- which they did. San Francisco hasn't won a World Series since, however. College athletics looked entirely different 13 years ago, to say the least. One of the biggest changes in college football lies in the implementation of the playoff system. Previously, the sport used the BCS rankings for 16 years to determine which two teams would play in the national championship game. That system had its fair share of controversies and came to a close following the 2013 campaign. Florida State and Auburn made sure the BCS era went out with a bang at the Rose Bowl. Facing a four-point deficit with 1:05 left, Heisman-winning quarterback Jameis Winston led the Seminoles down the field for a game-winning touchdown. Two plays later Florida State closed it out to win 34-31 and clinch its first national championship since 1999 in memorable fashion.

title: Liverpool games v Man United and Everton moved as Premier League confirm updated fixture details - Yahoo Sports
content: Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday. With the November international break now concluded, the Reds' next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January. The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches. On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool's games being moved. The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage. The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports). Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January. Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield. *FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we'll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won't be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola's side. Liverpool currently have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month. It's quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two). Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

title: NetChoice v. Rokita (Indiana) - NetChoice
content:
Case Status: Complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, Indianapolis Division
Latest Update: November 18, 2026 
Attorneys: Indiana has joined the age-verification discussion, siding with the U.K., Europe, and Australia. In other words, Indiana is imposing a one-size-fits-all mandate on everyone in the state who wants to use popular online speech services. NetChoice’s newest lawsuit challenges the social media provisions of HEA 1408, a law that will require covered websites to determine the age and Indiana residency of every user, adult or teen, before they can open or keep an account. Users will face repeated age checks for up to a decade, and even when parents give permission, the state, not families, will decide how teen accounts work. Federal courts have blocked similar laws in Arkansas, Utah, and Louisiana. This is an ID-for-Speech law, and it violates the First Amendment. Any user flagged as possibly under 16, adult or teen, has 30 days to prove their age or lose their account. They can prove it with parental consent or with “transactional data” such as mortgage, education, or employment records. The law requires platforms to delete parental-consent information but not the transactional data. That creates a honeypot for hackers and identity thieves and threatens the anonymous speech that many Americans rely on, including whistleblowers, abuse survivors, and users looking for sensitive health information. HEA 1408 also overrides parents instead of empowering them. Even with a parent’s permission, the state turns off personalized recommendations and disables features it labels “addictive.” Those are editorial choices the Supreme Court protected in Moody v. NetChoice. A parent can’t let their teen get recommendations for coding tutorials or college-prep content. Teens in foster care or living with relatives who aren’t their legal guardians could be cut off entirely. NetChoice’s Digital Safety Shield for America offers a better path forward with legal and meaningful solutions that protect families online without harming the rights of all Hoosiers. NetChoice’s complaint filed on November 18, 2026, in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, Indianapolis Division.

title: Ireland v South Africa: Hosts name Dan Sheehan at number eight for Nations Championship match - BBC
content: Sheehan's only previous game at number eight was Leinster's win over Munster last month Ireland captain Dan Sheehan has been named at number eight for Saturday's highly anticipated Nations Championship match against world champions South Africa in Dublin. Having won all 42 of his previous caps at hooker, the 28-year-old returns after recovering from a concussion to partner flankers Ryan Baird and Josh van der Flier in the back row. Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has faced an injury crisis at number eight with regular skipper Caelan Doris, Jack Conan, Sean Jansen and recent debutant James McNabney all ruled out. Nick Timoney, who was handed the jersey for last week's victory over Fiji, drops to the bench. With Doris and Conan unavailable, Sheehan anchored the scrum in Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster last month, but Saturday will be his first Test run-out in the back row. "Most people would agree that he [Sheehan]'s a world-class player, not just good," said Farrell, who did not wish to comment on South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus' six-match ban for questioning the integrity of match officials. "Throwing the ball in or scrummaging, his point of difference is in and around the field and how he plays the game with ball in hand or defensively, running lines and all of that. "That's suited to number eight. He was training there all last week because he was on the 12-day return-to-play protocols, so we had a bit of a head start there, and he played there recently. "He's very cool, calm and collected; there's no arrogance there whatsoever. Things don't bother him, so he takes it all in his stride, fully confident in his own ability." South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches Ireland fly-half Prendergast cleared to face South Africa Sheehan's move means that Ronan Kelleher keeps his place at hooker after starting the Fiji game, again joining props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong in the front row. After being rested last week, Joe McCarthy returns to the second row to partner Tadhg Beirne, with Van der Flier edging out Timoney for the number seven jersey. Sam Prendergast starts at fly-half after being cleared to face the Springboks on Wednesday, with Jamison Gibson-Park retained at scrum-half. Prendergast, 23, was cited for his hip-drop tackle on Fiji's Peceli Yato - which was not punished on the pitch - but an independent disciplinary panel ruled the challenge was not worthy of a red card. "Nothing's changed for us all week," Farrell said when asked about the possibility of a Prendergast ban. "There's always something going on, whether it's dealing with HIA (head injury assessment) injuries or incidents like we've had with Sam this week. "It (the hearing) was late on Tuesday night; we trained Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and Sam's done all of that so there's been no hiccups for us, let's say that." Robbie Henshaw and Stuart McCloskey both return to midfield after Farrell opted to pair Jamie Osborne and Bundee Aki in a new-look centre partnership against Fiji. However, Osborne was replaced by McCloskey in the third minute after sustaining a pectoral injury that has ruled him out of the South Africa game, while Aki drops to the bench. With Hugo Keenan returning to full-back for his 50th cap after sitting out the Fiji game, Mack Hansen switches to the left wing with Robert Baloucoune retained on the right. Tommy O'Brien, who scored two tries from the left wing against Fiji, drops out of the squad. Farrell has opted for a split of five forwards and three backs on the bench. Tom Stewart, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, James Ryan and Timoney provide pack cover with Craig Casey, Ciaran Frawley and Aki named as backline reinforcements. Nick Timoney (left) drops to the bench while Sam Prendergast (right) starts at fly-half after being cleared of foul play South Africa, who named their team on Monday, make five changes with record cap holder Eben Etzebeth recalled to the second row. Cameron Hanekom is named at number eight, replacing Jasper Wiese, who was handed a four-week suspension after being sent off for a dangerous clear-out in last week's defeat by France. Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw are named as the starting front row. Erasmus also named Nche, Marx and Louw to start the France game but swapped them out for Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit shortly before kick-off at the Stade de France. As part of the six-game ban handed down by World Rugby on Tuesday, Erasmus is not permitted to attend the Aviva Stadium encounter. The 54-year-old has since announced he will be hosting an online watchalong of the match while he watches from his team's Dublin hotel. Shane Horgan: Rassie Erasmus' language is 'Trumpian' South Africa sit second in the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings, a point adrift of New Zealand. A South Africa win over Ireland coupled with England beating the All Blacks (Saturday, 14:10 GMT) would be enough for Erasmus' side to seal a place in the 29 November final against the top-ranked northern hemisphere side at Twickenham. Ireland must beat the Springboks and hope France and England falter against Argentina and New Zealand to finish top. The Springboks won 24-13 at Aviva Stadium last year, their first victory over Ireland in Dublin since 2012. Ireland: H Keenan; R Baloucoune, R Henshaw, S McCloskey, M Hansen; S Prendergast, J Gibson-Park; A Porter, R Kelleher, T Furlong, J McCarthy, T Beirne, R Baird, J van der Flier, D Sheehan (capt). Replacements: T Stewart, T O'Toole, S Illo, J Ryan, N Timoney, C Casey, C Frawley, B Aki. title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya - UN News
content: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State. At the end of a three-hour ruling at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague, President Yuji Iwasawa of Japan also declared that Myanmar had failed to prevent and punish genocide, after detailing how Myanmar’s military had perpetrated “extreme violence” against mainly Muslim Rohingya communities in Rakhine state. UN Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed the judgment as a “powerful recognition of the Rohingya victims of genocide. It is a demonstration of international justice and a reaffirmation that impunity for such horrific acts must not stand.” The UN chief stressed that ending impunity in Myanmar and ensuring accountability remained essential to national reconciliation and added that the judgment “will be studied carefully within the United Nations. International law, including the Genocide Convention, must be respected by all.” The ruling establishes that Myanmar’s security forces “and other State organs” intentionally committed specifically prohibited acts covered by Article II of the Genocide Convention. These are Article II(a) – killing members of a group, Article II(b) – causing seriously bodily or mental harm to members of the group and Article II(d) – imposing measures intended to prevent births within the group. The ICJ ruling came after studying graphic evidence and testimonies provided by survivors and reports from international investigators describing how Rohingya villages and bridges had been set alight and bulldozed, with men and boys executed and girls and women raped during military clearance operations in northern Rakhine in 2017. The military clearance operations also involved the murder of infants, which “supports the inference that Myanmar’s security forces acted with the intent to prevent births among the group”, Judge Iwasawa continued. Delivering the court’s ruling, the ICJ President described how the mainly Muslim Rohingya living in Rakhine state in western Myanmar had been the target of successive clearance operations by the State military, after decades of intercommunal violence. The 2017 clearance operations prompted widespread international condemnation after some 700,000 Rohingya fled northern Rakhine state across the border to Bangladesh. According to the court, an estimated 10,000 Rohingya were killed during the clearance operations, citing supporting evidence. The case at the ICJ was initiated by The Gambia in November 2019; it has become one of the most closely watched proceedings before the world’s highest court. Related to the exodus and mass killings, rape and other sexual violence, the court heard testimonies from three witnesses from the Rakhine state villages of Min Gyi, Chut Pyin and Maung Nu. In addition, one witness called by Myanmar gave an account of an attack in which Rohingya insurgents the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) allegedly killed around 100 civilians. The court heard that nearly 400 villages – approximately 40 per cent of the almost 1,000 villages in the three townships of northern Rakhine state – were partially or totally destroyed during and after the 2017 clearance operations. “Bulldozing and large-scale terrain clearance often followed the destruction…in turn, rapid construction took place on the cleared sites, including security installations, new villages and houses, and other civilian infrastructure,” Judge Iwasawa explained. As a consequence of these breaches of the Genocide Convention, the Court ordered Myanmar: to cease any ongoing violations by enacting legislation giving full effect to its obligations under the Convention; to take immediate and effective steps to investigate all persons reasonably suspected of having committed acts contrary to the Convention and, if warranted, to prosecute and punish them. In addition, the ruling orders Myanmar to provide assurances and guarantees of non-repetition and prevent similar violations from occurring in the future; to adopt measures of restitution in the interest of the Rohingya, including allowing the safe, voluntary and dignified return to their place of residence and reunification of families for the Rohingya who were displaced as a result of the Respondent’s wrongful acts, whether they were displaced within Myanmar or abroad; and to compensate the Rohingya group and its members for the damage caused. Finally, the Court decided that the question of the amount and the modalities of compensation or other reparation should be determined in a subsequent phase of the proceedings, and that, to that end, Myanmar should transmit to it, within two years of today’s Judgment, a report on the measures of restitution it has adopted and the amount and modalities of compensation. The judgment is final, binding on the parties to the case and without appeal. Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro (filed 1993; judgment 2007): The Court ruled that Serbia did not commit genocide itself, but found that it violated the Genocide Convention by failing to prevent the 1995 Srebrenica genocide and failing to punish or transfer perpetrators. Croatia v. Serbia (filed 1999; judgment 2015): The Court dismissed both Croatia's main claim and Serbia's counterclaim, finding that neither state proved the specific genocidal intent (dolus specialis) required under the Convention during the Croatian War of Independence. Public hearings opened on Monday at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in a landmark case brought by the Gambia against Myanmar, alleging violations of the Genocide Convention over the military’s treatment of the Rohingya minority. Myanmar on Friday rejected allegations of genocide against the Rohingya minority, telling the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that the Gambia’s case rests on “unsubstantiated allegations,” as public hearings continued in a landmark case on the application of the Genocide Convention.

title: Gambia v. Myanmar: The Bottom Line - EJIL: Talk!
content: The ICJ just delivered its historic judgment in Gambia v. Myanmar. By 9 votes to 6, it found that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It also made a number of other findings, which I will not discuss here. As a matter of remedies, the Court ordered Myanmar to institute a programme of restitution and compensation, with a two-year deadline to provide a report to the Court on what exactly it has done. This is the first time that the Court has found that a state has committed genocide. I am sure this finding will be enormously impactful on the Rohingya survivors, who will find in this pronouncement a measure of justice that they have long been waiting for. That said, this was clearly a hard case for the Court. It is not usually split so heavily, and in cases of this importance it works hard on maintaining consensus. And the judgment is followed by a set of 11 (!) separate opinions. The most important one of these is the Joint dissenting opinion of Vice-President Sebutinde, Judges Tomka, Abraham, Xue, Nolte and Judge ad hoc Kress. Obviously I have not had the time to fully digest it. But at first glance, the disagreement among the judges is essentially as follows: the majority has preserved fidelity to its prior judgments in the Bosnian and Croatian genocide cases against Serbia, but that fidelity is at times skin-deep. In particular, the joint dissent accused the majority of the Court of reading the notion of destruction in Article II of the Genocide Convention a bit more flexibly, and, even more so, that it has adopted a substantially more flexible approach to evidence. Thus, even though the Court adheres to its prior jurisprudence in saying that the standard of proof is that of fully convincing evidence, and that to infer genocidal intent from circumstantial evidence this has to be the ‘only reasonable inference’ available, in practice the factors it takes into account are such that they blur the difference between genocide and ethnic cleansing/crimes against humanity of forcible displacement and persecution. This is the core disagreement among the judges. Again, to have a more informed sense of whether it is the majority or the dissent that have the better argument here one needs to digest all the opinions properly. The key point is that the ICJ in the Bosnian and Croatian cases worked off the judgments of the ICTY. There was an obvious incentive to main consistency with them, whereas here it was mainly relying on the work of fact-finding and investigative mechanisms established by the UN. For the dissent, the sum total of the evidence assembled by these bodies, even if taken as fully proven, does not support the ‘only reasonable inference’ of genocidal intent that would be established conclusively. Obviously, this disagreement among the judges has bearing on pending genocide cases before the Court, including the litigation regarding Gaza. So does, obviously, the changing composition of the bench. Thus, while I think it is fair to say that the Court did not expand the definition of genocide in this case, or at least did not so do beyond the limits of reasonable interpretation, it is also fair to say that its approach to fact-finding is more flexible than in the past. Whether this is justified or not, and whether the outcome of the Bosnian and Croatian cases would have been different had this approach been applied to them, is clearly a matter of reasonable disagreement. This is where the judges ended up at – and notably the dissenting group includes the judges who sat on the Bosnian and Croatian cases. I will leave things here. We will have many more posts on GvM in the days to come, and there are plenty of other issues in the judgment that warrant careful analysis other than this bottom line (e.g. regarding direct and public incitement to genocide, reparations, and so forth). title: Stephanie V. Love received an American Academy in Rome award - University of Pittsburgh
content: Stephanie V. Love, an assistant professor in the Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences’ Department of Anthropology, is a recipient of the 2026-27 Rome Prize, awarded by the American Academy in Rome. Love, one of 31 fellows, is co-leading the project “Relics of the Future: Migrating Politics and the Making of the ‘New World Order’ in Post-Cold War Rome” with Yale University’s Amara Lakhous. During the fellowship, Love and Lakhous will examine how “migrating politics” have shaped Roman, Italian and European politics today by investigating Rome’s first migrant-led social movement, known as the Pantanella or Shish Mahal, led by manual laborers from South Asia and North Africa who occupied an abandoned pasta factory in 1990.
